title: Stack machine interpreter
prompt:
Run the programs given at the end on a small stack machine. A program is a list of lines numbered from 1. A line is either a label, written `NAME:`, which only marks a position and is not an instruction, or one instruction. The machine has a stack of integers (empty at the start) and a separate return stack, and it executes the instructions one after another, starting with the first line. The instructions:
- `push N`: push the integer N (which may be negative).
- `pop`: remove the top value. `dup`: push a copy of the top value. `swap`: exchange the top two values. `over`: push a copy of the second value from the top.
- `add`, `sub`, `mul`, `div`, `mod`: remove the top value b, then the new top value a, and push a + b, a - b, a * b, the whole number of times b fits into a (the remainder discarded), or that remainder, respectively. In these programs the operands of `div` and `mod` are never negative.
- `print`: remove the top value and print it on its own line.
- `jmp NAME`: continue with the first instruction after the label NAME.
- `jz NAME`: remove the top value; if it is 0, continue after the label NAME, otherwise continue with the next line.
- `call NAME`: push the position of the next line on the return stack, then continue after the label NAME. `ret`: remove the top position from the return stack and continue there.
- `halt`: stop the program.
A program also stops after its last line. A program stops with an error, printing one line, in these cases: an instruction needs more values than the stack holds (`pop`, `dup`, `print` and `jz` need 1; `swap`, `over`, `add`, `sub`, `mul`, `div` and `mod` need 2): `error at line N: stack underflow`; `div` or `mod` with b = 0: `error at line N: division by zero`; `ret` with an empty return stack: `error at line N: return without call`. N is the line number of the failing instruction, and a failing instruction changes nothing. Also, a program may execute at most 100 instructions (labels do not count): when it has executed 100 instructions and is about to execute another one, it stops instead, printing the line `error: step limit`.
For each program K, print `program K`, then its output, then, after it stops for any reason, the line `stack: ` followed by the values left on the stack from the bottom to the top, separated by spaces, or `stack: empty`.
The programs, each as its lines in order:
- program 1: `push 9875`, `call digits`, `print`, `push 406`, `call digits`, `print`, `halt`, `digits:`, `push 0`, `loop:`, `over`, `jz done`, `over`, `push 10`, `mod`, `add`, `swap`, `push 10`, `div`, `swap`, `jmp loop`, `done:`, `swap`, `pop`, `ret`
- program 2: `push 5`, `push 3`, `sub`, `dup`, `print`, `push 7`, `swap`, `sub`, `print`, `push -4`, `ret`, `print`
- program 3: `push 3`, `top:`, `dup`, `print`, `push 2`, `mul`, `jmp top`
- program 4: `push 6`, `push 4`, `call f`, `print`, `f:`, `over`, `over`, `mod`, `jz g`, `push 0`, `div`, `g:`, `ret`
- program 5: `push 1`, `push 2`, `swap`, `over`, `add`, `add`, `mul`, `push 8`
